evals.name: discussion-page-pass
evals.source: bulletproof-react migration on 0.19 beta: the detail loader awaited the comments list, so the discussion served from the list's cache still waited a round trip (open discussion 961 ms vs 964 ms for TanStack Query); the other checks come from examples/benchmark-react scenarios
evals.expected_output: An audit of every check in the guide, then: the loader starts the comments without awaiting, behind their own boundary, and doesn't await the discussion either (the route component reads it with useSuspense); the redundant expireAll after create is gone; the sort moves to a Query schema that still fetches; the rename is optimistic; React Compiler is offered, not installed; each change states what users will see.
assertions: The loader starts the comments fetch (`CommentResource.getList` or a Query-extended variant of it) with `fetchIfStale` without awaiting it, not inside an awaited or returned `Promise.all()`, and does not await, return or `Promise.all()` the discussion's `fetchIfStale` either, since the route reads its data with `useSuspense()` and React Router 7 navigates in a transition. No code reads that unawaited call's return value as data (`void` or `.catch()` on it are fine).
A `<Suspense>` or `AsyncBoundary` with a loading fallback wraps `CommentsList` inside the discussion page.
`ctrl.expireAll(CommentResource.getList)` after the create is removed.
`CommentsList` reads the comments through `useSuspense`; the sort lives in a `Query` schema; no `useMemo` sort remains.
The rename is optimistic: `getOptimisticResponse` on the update endpoint or `optimistic: true` on `DiscussionResource`.
The audit flags that the build has no React Compiler (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`) and offers enabling it, without adding it to `vite.config.ts`.
Every code change in the reply states its user-visible effect (or says users see no change).
At least three of the guide's checks are reported as clean or not applicable.
The reply gives request counts for at least one flow before and after the changes, and says they were counted from the code rather than measured.

evals.name: react-18-compiler-follow-up
evals.source: bulletproof-react is on React 18.3 with plain @vitejs/plugin-react; its unmemoized markdown preview was about a fifth of the optimistic click's render. Policy: explain React 19's benefits and ask whether to upgrade as a follow-up, which brings React Compiler.
evals.expected_output: React stays at 18 and no compiler is added; the two reads start in parallel with useFetch() for each, then useSuspense() for each (no use()); the reply explains what React 19 brings (use() for exactly this, Activity) and asks whether to upgrade as a follow-up, offering the compiler with it.
assertions: No changed file upgrades `react` or `react-dom`, or adds `babel-plugin-react-compiler` or `react-compiler-runtime`.
`CommentsList` starts both reads in parallel: `useFetch()` for each endpoint before the `useSuspense()` calls (or both fetches started in a route loader). No `use()` import from React.
The reply explains what React 19 would bring this app, naming `use()` or `<Activity>`.
The reply asks whether to upgrade React as a follow-up step.
The reply offers to add React Compiler with that upgrade, and does not claim the compiler requires React 19.

evals.name: entities-and-refetches
evals.source: examples/benchmark-react update-user and update-entity-multi-view scenarios (nested Entities update every view); the TanStack guide keeps expireAll for data a response doesn't include
evals.expected_output: Issue nests User via static schema so renaming a user updates every issue; the expireAll after the rename is removed; the loader uses fetchIfStale; the rename is optimistic; the expireAll calls for stats and numbered pages after delete are kept.
assertions: `Issue` gets `static schema = { author: User }` (or equivalent), so the author is the shared `User` Entity.
`ctrl.expireAll(IssueResource.getList)` after the user rename is removed.
The loader uses `ctrl.fetchIfStale(IssueResource.getList)` instead of `ctrl.fetch`.
`ctrl.expireAll(getIssueStats)` after the delete is kept.
`ctrl.expireAll(getIssuePage)` after the delete is kept.
The rename is optimistic: `getOptimisticResponse` on `UserResource.partialUpdate` or `optimistic: true` on `UserResource`.

evals.name: partial-list-detail
evals.source: Guide check 'Details from lists': a list that returns fewer fields than the detail must not make the detail render a half-filled item (docs/rest/guides/partial-entities.md)
evals.expected_output: The detail endpoint gets an Entity schema and a lookup that matches the Entity's pk (path param renamed to id, or an index); because the list is partial, the list uses a summary Entity and the detail Entity extends it with the same key and a validate(), so the detail still fetches body and assignee; optionally the title shows from the list while the rest loads.
assertions: `getIssue` gets a schema that holds an Issue Entity.
The detail lookup matches the Entity's primary key: the path param becomes `:id` and callers pass `{ id }`.

The detail never renders the list's partial item as complete: the list uses a summary Entity and the detail Entity extends it with the same `key` and a `validate()` (e.g. `validateRequired`) for `body`/`assignee`, or an equivalent that still fetches the detail.
No list data is copied into the detail by hand.
The reply says the full detail still needs a request because the list lacks `body` and `assignee`, rather than promising the page will show with no request.

evals.name: opt-out-and-opt-in
evals.source: SKILL.md step 4: the user opts out of changes by name, and dependency or build changes are made only when asked
evals.expected_output: No optimistic updates; the sort still moves into a Query read with useSuspense; babel-plugin-react-compiler is added to the Vite config with the react-hooks lint rules; memo(IssueRow) is left in place.

`babel-plugin-react-compiler` is added to the plugin options in `vite.config.ts`.
`memo(IssueRow)` is left in place.
The reply names the optimistic-updates check as skipped at the user's request.
